Function map

Source: vignettes/function-naming.Rmd
function-naming.Rmd

This page helps you find the function for a task and the methods that read its result. It explains how the names are built, then lists the functions by task and the methods by result. It runs no analysis. The guides that use these functions run on The Cornwall GP example data. The spax() interface and the allocation model are experimental and may change in later versions.

How the names work

The prefix says what a function is for, and the rest names the thing:

  • spax() runs a model specification on prepared data: an FCA (floating catchment area) index or an allocation model. spax_<model>() runs one model in one call from raw inputs: spax_e2sfca() and the other FCA indices, spax_huff() and spax_clm().
  • prep_ prepares data: prep_data().
  • spec_ specifies a model without data: spec_clm() (the conditional logit model, CLM: facilities plus an outside option, the choice of none of them), spec_huff() (the Huff model: facilities only) and the FCA indices spec_2sfca(), spec_e2sfca(), spec_m2sfca(), spec_3sfca() and spec_huff2sfca(), compared in Which FCA index?.
  • decay_ declares how weight falls with travel time: decay_gaussian(), decay_exponential(), decay_power(), decay_custom() and decay_kernel(). decay_step() and decay_inverse() are for FCA indices only.
  • obs_ declares observed counts: obs_flows() and obs_totals().
  • calc_, gather_ and spread_ are the building blocks of an index. calc_travel_time() and calc_demand() compute inputs.
  • transform_, rasterize_, update_ and sample_ move area totals onto a grid, and read_ and save_ read and write files.
  • <verb>_allocation() are the steps that spax() runs underneath for an allocation model, such as fit_allocation().

A model keeps its name as the suffix: spec_huff() specifies the Huff model, and spax_huff() runs it. check_fit(), compare_fits() and bootstrap_fit() work on fitted results: a result of spax(), or a model and its fit from the steps. They are also named check_allocation(), compare_allocations() and bootstrap_allocation(): each pair is one function.

Find a function by task

Every exported function appears on this page, most of them in this table.

Task Functions What you get
Read the example grids read_spax_example() A population or travel raster
Prepare inputs for any model prep_data() Prepared data: numeric inputs, or raster data
Spread area totals over a grid transform_pmf(), transform_demand() A grid of shares that sum to 1 (transform_pmf()), or with density = TRUE counts that keep each area’s total (transform_demand())
Reweight a grid pattern by an area rate rasterize_demand(), or its parts transform_likelihood() and update_pmf() A grid of shares or of counts
Draw random point patterns from a grid sample_pmf() Counts per cell, one layer per draw
Compute travel times over a friction surface calc_travel_time() A travel matrix or raster
Compute demand from population groups and rates calc_demand() A demand raster or vector
Compute an FCA index spax() with spec_2sfca(), spec_e2sfca(), spec_m2sfca(), spec_3sfca() or spec_huff2sfca() On raster data, a spax result with the index raster; on numeric data, the index at each origin
Compute an FCA index in one call spax_2sfca(), spax_e2sfca(), spax_m2sfca(), spax_3sfca(), spax_huff2sfca() A spax result with the index raster
Choose the decay of an FCA index decay_gaussian(), decay_exponential() or decay_power() with a number or a raster sigma; decay_step(), decay_inverse(), decay_custom() A decay for the specification
Build an index from its parts calc_decay(), calc_normalize(), calc_choice(), gather_weighted(), gather_demand(), spread_weighted(), spread_access(), compute_access() Weights, demand per facility and index rasters
Save and read an FCA result with its rasters save_spax(), read_spax() Files on disk, and the result read back
Specify an allocation model spec_clm(), spec_huff() with decay_gaussian(), decay_exponential(), decay_power() or decay_custom() A model specification
Declare a decay curve of your own decay_kernel(), used through decay_custom() A kernel declaration
Declare observed counts obs_flows(), obs_totals() Observed counts with the loss that fits them
Fit an allocation model, or run it at fixed parameter values spax(); from raw inputs in one call, spax_clm() or spax_huff() An allocation result
Predict at other origins predict() on an allocation result Probabilities, outside shares and flows by origin
Check what the data identify check_fit() The fit beside simpler allocations
Compare fitted models compare_fits() One row per fit
Put intervals on a fit to facility totals bootstrap_fit() Estimates, intervals and every attempt
Run the allocation steps one at a time prepare_allocation(), clm_allocation(), huff_allocation(), fit_allocation(), evaluate_allocation(), predict_allocation() Prepared inputs, a declared model, a fit, an evaluation or a prediction

Read a result

Each result has methods that read it. None of them refits the model or resamples the bootstrap. An output that a fit did not keep, such as the flows of a fit to facility totals, is computed when you ask for it.

Result Made by Read it with
FCA index on a grid (spax) spax() on raster data, spax_e2sfca() and the other one-call functions print(), summary(), plot(); $accessibility is the index raster
FCA index on numeric data (spax_access_values) spax() on numeric data print(), summary(), as.data.frame(); $access is a matrix with one row per origin
Allocation result (spax_allocation) spax(), spax_clm(), spax_huff() print(), summary(), coef(), fitted(), predict(), as.data.frame() with type "parameters", "facilities", "origins", "flows" or "starts"
Prediction predict(), predict_allocation() $outputs holds what you asked for; $validity gives each origin a status, such as valid, unknown_travel or known_absence, saying whether its values could be computed
Check check_fit() print(), as.data.frame()
Comparison compare_fits() print(), as.data.frame() with type "fits" or "zones"
Bootstrap bootstrap_fit() print(), summary(), plot(), as.data.frame() with type "estimates", "draws" or "starts"
Fit from the steps (ae_multistart_fit) fit_allocation() print(), summary(), coef(), fitted(), plot(), as.data.frame()

An index raster is read with terra, for example terra::values() or terra::as.data.frame(). Reading results says how to save each kind of result.
